assets.name: Palais Galliera
assets.axes: X east / Y up / Z south
assets.attribution: Open Landmarks; contains © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0
assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: The OSM outline fixes the palace, lateral galleries and semicircular rear courtyard, preserving its central void. The mapped gallery part is 7 m tall; the remaining palace uses the outline 13 m height.

The inspected CC0 photo references/00.jpg establishes the garden front with three monumental glazed arches, engaged columns, strong horizontal cornices, roof parapet and lower columned wings. Main facade arch/pier dimensions are proportional inferences fitted to the mapped south facade.

The mapped low gallery is represented as an open colonnade beneath its continuous 7 m roof. Repeated column locations and semicircular gallery rhythm are inferred from the plan and visible lateral colonnade; the rear side is not shown by the selected photograph.

The wall plane is set 0.45 m inside the mapped outer ornament envelope to expose engaged columns; foundation, parapet and roof retain the mapped extremities. The palace roof is a flat grey surface enclosed by a shallow stone parapet. Balustrade sculpture, inscriptions, fine capitals and ironwork are omitted. Windows use the standard light-blue palette; no photographic textures are used.

assets.name: Église Saint-Pierre de Montmartre

assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: The ten OSM building parts supply every major footprint, roof type and height: 16 m nave, 13 m apsidal/transept roofs and 26 m bell-tower apex. The original source outline and all part coordinates are retained.

Two inspected east photographs show paired open Romanesque belfry arches above a lower stone stage. The tower uses actual arched voids instead of dark window panels; 0.65 m wall thickness and arch dimensions are visual inferences.

Arched light-blue nave/apse glazing, narrow cornices and mapped 7 m buttress volumes suggest the facade rhythm. The church interior, sculptures, tombs, individual masonry and small roof cross are omitted.

assets.name: Théâtre Marigny
assets.axes: X east / Y up / Z south
assets.attribution: Open Landmarks; contains © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL-1.0
assets.licenseScope: CC BY applies to original artistic contributions only; ODbL applies to OSM-derived spatial data. Reference photographs retain their own licenses.
modelingNotes: Three OSM parts define the complete 6 m foyer skirt, the polygonal 12 m auditorium and the central 15 m roof lantern. Eaves follow the tagged 1/3/1.5 m roof heights.

The inspected CC BY-SA 3.0 reference 00 shows the Théâtre Marigny behind the Fontaine du Cirque: blank upper auditorium panels, strong cornices, low foyer windows and a raised central lantern are retained. The fountain is outside the modeled building and omitted.

Upper parts start at the lower eave/roof datum; internal hidden roofs are removed beneath the auditorium. The lower skirt roof uses a narrow setback instead of the coarse whole-building pyramidal tag, an explicit inference from the low surrounding roof in the photograph.

Pilaster width, cornice thickness and repeated foyer/lantern windows are map-scale inferences. Inscriptions, ornate cresting, sculpture and fine lantern grille are omitted; the standard grey roof and light-blue glazing palette replaces photographic colors.
